correctness.rationale: The exact invariant-measure transfer kernel gives P_N g_m=(N+x)/(m+x); a trigamma identity evaluates P_N x and its derivative -1/(2N)+O(N^-2). Stochastic ordering of branch kernels yields a Lipschitz contraction through their ordered Wasserstein-1 distance. Induction controls the N^-k affine slope and O(N^-k-1) remainder at each fixed lag. Stationary transfer duality and the explicit indicator-coordinate covariance give the stated coefficient, with boundaries and quantifiers checked. The extracted verifier passes 56 independent finite exact/numerical tests but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed main claim is the exact nonzero N^k-scaled covariance limit for every fixed lag and all interior scaled thresholds. Prior Lascu Proposition 4.2 already has monotonicity reversal and 1/(N+1) variation contraction (hence alternating correlation signs), which are not claimed new. Relevant Gauss–Kuzmin and two-dimensional convergence papers were inspected. Those estimates do not state or directly imply the sharp coefficient 2^-k with both threshold amplitudes. Residual possibility of an unindexed spectral asymptotic remains.
residual_risks: The published Gauss–Kuzmin bound already implies a nonsharp O(N^-k) rate and the sign, so neither alone is original.
An earlier or unindexed large-numerator perturbation of transfer-operator spectra could reproduce the exact coefficient.
Priority comparison is not independent historical certification.

value.rationale: The invariant digit process is a canonical ergodic dynamical observable. Exact fixed-lag dependence coefficients reveal a universal asymptotic factor -1/(2N) per lag and nontrivial threshold geometry, rather than qualitative contraction. The parameter N varies through a natural unbounded family, not arbitrary data slices. The result resolves the leading dependence amplitude at every fixed separation; no downstream theorem is required. Fixed N and growing lag, unbounded digit values and nonstationary laws are explicitly outside scope.
